features.description: `scripts/live-run.sh <command…>` runs a one-off worker command in the image the worker container was deployed from (its `org.opencontainers.image.revision` label), and `scripts/live-check.sh` is the Check through it; both tested with a stub docker, never run live.
steps: `scripts/live-run.sh` (bash, `set -euo pipefail`) reads `docker inspect -f '{{index .Config.Labels "org.opencontainers.image.revision"}}' dj-worker-1`, refuses with exit 1 and a one-line reason when the container is missing, the revision is empty or `dev`, or `docker image inspect dj-crates:<rev>` fails; otherwise prints `live-run: image dj-crates:<rev>` first, then runs `GIT_SHA=<rev> docker compose --project-directory /srv/docker run --rm --no-deps worker <command…>`. The revision in the tag is the 10-char form `scripts/deploy.sh` uses (`git rev-parse --short=10`): if the label holds the full sha, truncate to 10; document which one deploy.sh writes (read deploy/compose.yml's `labels:` for the worker service).
`scripts/live-run.sh --print <command…>` prints the exact command it would run and exits 0 without running docker compose.
`scripts/live-check.sh` runs, through live-run.sh, `sh -c 'python3 -m scripts.export_playlists export && python3 -m scripts.export_playlists check'` and exits with its status.

tests/test_live_run.py, in the style of tests/test_deploy_script.py (a stub `docker` first on PATH that records argv to $DOCKER_LOG and answers `inspect` from an env var such as $STUB_REVISION): the happy path runs compose with `GIT_SHA=<rev>` in its environment, `run --rm --no-deps worker` and the command verbatim; each refusal (missing container, empty label, `dev`, image not present) exits 1 with its reason and never calls `compose`; `--print` calls no `compose`; live-check.sh passes the two export_playlists commands.
No test and no step of this feature calls the real docker: `grep -rn 'docker' tests/test_live_run.py` shows only the stub path.

CLAUDE.md 'Check' names `scripts/live-check.sh` as the Check (keeping the long form as what it runs); docs/worker.md 'Duplicate cleanup' trash commands use `scripts/live-run.sh python3 -m scripts.duplicate_cleanup trash …` instead of the bare `docker compose run --rm --no-deps worker …`; the pivot spec gets `D45 *default*`: live one-off commands run in the deployed image, resolved from the worker container's revision label (`grep -n 'D45' docs/specs/2026-10-17-amperfy-pivot.md`).
Commit `R2-01: live-run.sh and live-check.sh run one-offs in the deployed image`.

features.description: Before rewriting a changed `.m3u8`, the export keeps the previous file in `_playlists/.history/<YYYY-MM-DD>/`, pruned after 30 days; pruning never touches anything outside `.history/`.
steps: scripts/export_playlists.py `export`: when `target` exists and its text differs, copy it to `out_dir/.history/<today>/<fname>` before the atomic replace, only if that history file does not exist yet (the first version of the day is the one kept); an unchanged file is never copied; a new playlist (no target) makes no history.

`prune_history(out_dir, today, days=30)` removes `.history/<date>/` directories whose date is older than `today - 30 days`, only directories named like a date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), and only under `out_dir/.history/`; it is called at the end of `export`; a `.history` that does not exist is fine; a symlink inside `.history` is not followed.
`check` and the `stale` list ignore `.history/` (they already glob only `*.m3u8` in `out_dir`; a test proves a history file is not reported stale).

tests/test_export_playlists.py: a second export after a playlist change leaves `.history/<today>/<fname>` equal to the first file's text; a third change the same day keeps the first; `prune_history` with a 31-day-old directory removes it, keeps a 29-day-old one, keeps `.history/notes/` and a file in `out_dir` with an old mtime, and never deletes outside `.history` (assert the music dir and the live `.m3u8` files are untouched); the worker's export tick (tests/test_worker.py) produces the history file.
docs/worker.md 'What it does each tick' step 4 mentions the history and the 30-day prune; `docs/hard-won-facts.md` line on `.m3u8` exports notes the history as the restore source.
Commit `R5-02: .m3u8 history before each rewrite, pruned after 30 days`.

features.description: `strip_trackno` keeps a bare leading 'NN ' when the rest no longer fits the wanted title ('99 Luftballons', M9 §8b), and a MusicBrainz recording whose version is only in its disambiguation fits a file titled with that version (§8c, recall only).
steps: sourcing/identity.py: `strip_trackno(s, wanted: str | None = None)`: with a wanted title, a bare `NN ` prefix (digits and a space, no `-`, `.` or `_` separator) is stripped only when the remainder still `loose`-matches the wanted title's start; `03 - Good Times`, `03. Good Times`, `A1 Good Times` strip as before; `99 Luftballons` with wanted `99 Luftballons` stays; `01 99 Luftballons` becomes `99 Luftballons`. `parse_filename(basename, artist, wanted=None)` passes it through; sourcing/scorer.py and sourcing/fetch.py pass the wanted title where they parse candidates.

features.description: The crates service serves the identity rows and records choices: `GET /api/identity` and `POST /api/identity/choice` write `identity-choices.json` in the identity dir and log an `identity_pick` event with `decided_by=michael`.
steps: crates/service.py `Config` gets `identity_dir` from `CRATES_IDENTITY_DIR` (default `/data/identity`); a new module crates/identity_view.py (stdlib) loads the proposal JSON, builds the rows of the plan's shape (with `suggested` and `songId` via `scripts.export_playlists._path_ids` on `NAVIDROME_DB` when set), reads and writes `identity-choices.json` atomically (tmp + replace) and never writes anywhere else than `identity_dir`.

Routes: `GET /api/identity` → `{"created", "counts", "rows": [...]}` (404 with a plain message when no proposal file exists); `GET /api/identity?class=ambiguous` filters; `POST /api/identity/choice` with the plan's rules: 409 for accept/choose on `conflict`/`error`, 400 for a `choose` mbid not among the row's candidates or an unknown path, 200 with the stored choice otherwise; each accepted POST logs event `identity_pick` (`detail` = `<class> <path>: accept|choose <mbid>|skip`, `decided_by=michael` recorded in the detail or a column that `store.events` already has).

tests/test_identity_api.py: a tmp identity dir with a small proposal JSON in the real schema (made by running `identity_backfill.propose` on the suite's audio fixtures with a scripted MusicBrainz client, or copied from such a run), `CrateServer` on the fake; the rows, the suggestion rule (exactly one candidate on the file's own album → `suggested`; two or none → null), each refusal, the choices file after two clicks (the second replaces the first for the same path), the event, and that nothing is written outside the identity dir (list tmp_path).

features.description: `identity_backfill apply --choices <file>` merges the picker's choices into the proposal rows with the existing candidate check; tested dry-run only on fixtures.
steps: scripts/identity_backfill.py: `apply(..., choices: Path | None)` reads `identity-choices.json`; per row: `skip` → not selected; `choose <mbid>` → the row's `choose` is set (the existing `_intended` check refuses an mbid not among `candidates`, message unchanged); `accept` → the row is selected even when its class is outside `--classes` (only `search`, `ambiguous`, `none` rows: a choice on `conflict`/`error` is refused with `choices: <path> is <class>; refused`); a path in the choices file that is not in the proposal is reported and ignored; the dry-run output names which rows came from choices.
The CLI: `apply <proposal> --choices <file> --dry-run`; the file's `decided_by` is carried into the apply log lines (`decided_by: michael`).

tests/test_identity_backfill.py: on fixtures, dry-run with a choices file: an accepted `search` row is listed as would-write, a chosen `ambiguous` row shows the chosen id, a skipped row is absent, a wrong mbid is refused with the existing message, a conflict choice is refused, and nothing on disk changes (tags re-read equal); without `--choices` behaviour is unchanged (existing tests green).
docs/worker.md 'Identity backfill' gets the `--choices` form and docs/how-ids-work.md one paragraph on the picker.
